chapters.title: Jeremiah Called Before Birth
chapters.synopsis: The Lord tells young Jeremiah that he knew and sanctified him before he was formed in the womb and ordained him a prophet to the nations. Jeremiah protests that he is only a child, but the Lord touches his mouth and shows him a seething pot from the north, a sign of coming judgment on Judah.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah dates his call under Josiah

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Ordained before birth; the seething pot

chapters.title: Israel's Forsaken First Love
chapters.synopsis: The Lord recalls the kindness of Israel's youth and grieves that she has forsaken him, the fountain of living waters, for broken cisterns and idols. He indicts Judah for a faithlessness worse than any nation, chasing after strangers while denying her guilt.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Forsaking the fountain of living waters

chapters.title: A Plea to Return
chapters.synopsis: The Lord likens faithless Israel to a wife who has played the harlot yet is invited to return. He promises that if she repents he will heal her backslidings and gather her with Judah to Zion, giving shepherds after his own heart.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The harlot wife's faithlessness

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Return, ye backsliding children

chapters.title: The Foe from the North
chapters.synopsis: The Lord calls Judah to circumcise her heart and put away her idols, or judgment will come like a lion out of his thicket. Jeremiah sees the land laid waste and his own heart in anguish, for the whole nation faces destroyer armies from the north.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Circumcise your hearts, O Judah

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Vision of the destroyer from the north

chapters.title: None That Doeth Justly
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sends Jeremiah searching Jerusalem's streets for one man who executes judgment, but finds none among rich or poor who have not broken the yoke of covenant. Because they have forsaken the Lord for false prophets and unbridled sin, a nation from far will devour their harvest.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: No one that seeketh truth is found

chapters.title: Flee for Safety, O Children
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sounds an alarm for Jerusalem to flee, for a besieging army approaches like shepherds pitching tents against the city. Prophets and priests heal the hurt of the people slightly, crying peace when there is no peace, and the ancient paths of goodness are refused.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Siege approaches; false peace of the prophets

chapters.title: The Temple Sermon
chapters.synopsis: Standing in the temple gate, Jeremiah warns the people not to trust the lying words, 'the temple of the Lord,' while they steal, murder, and burn incense to Baal. The Lord recalls Shiloh's ruin as proof that the house bearing his name will not shield a people who will not amend their ways.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Trust not the lying words, the temple of the Lord

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Do not pray for this people; Shiloh's warning

chapters.title: No Balm in Gilead
chapters.synopsis: The Lord laments a people who do not turn from their wicked course even as the stork knows her appointed times, while scribes falsely handle the law. Jeremiah's own heart is faint within him, and he cries out that though there is balm in Gilead, no physician has healed his people.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A people who will not turn

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Is there no balm in Gilead

chapters.title: A Fountain of Tears
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah wishes his head were waters that he might weep for the slain of his people, so deep has treachery and deceit become among neighbors and brothers. The Lord declares that the wise, mighty, and rich should glory only in understanding and knowing him, for Judah's uncircumcised heart brings lamentation and dispersion.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: A fountain of tears for the slain

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Glory only in knowing the Lord

chapters.title: Idols of Wood and the Living God
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah contrasts the dumb idols of the nations, decked with silver and gold but unable to speak or walk, with the living God who made the earth by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens. He prays that the Lord correct his people with judgment, not in anger, lest they be brought to nothing.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Idols of wood versus the living God

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah prays for correction, not wrath

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.synopsis: The Lord reminds Jeremiah of the covenant sworn to the fathers who came out of Egypt, a covenant Judah and Israel have broken by following other gods. When Jeremiah's own kinsmen at Anathoth plot to kill him for prophesying, the Lord promises to bring evil upon them that they cannot escape.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The broken covenant of the fathers

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The men of Anathoth conspire against him

chapters.title: Why Do the Wicked Prosper
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah asks the Lord why the way of the wicked prospers while he suffers for righteousness, and the Lord answers that harder trials still lie ahead. Judah's own shepherds have marred the Lord's pleasant portion, yet mercy is promised even to the nations that will learn the ways of his people.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah questions the prosperity of the wicked

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Judgment on evil neighbors; mercy offered

chapters.title: The Marred Linen Girdle
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah buries a linen girdle by the Euphrates until it rots, a sign that the pride of Judah will likewise be marred and made profitable for nothing. The Lord warns the king and queen mother that captivity draws near, for a people accustomed to evil cannot easily do good.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The sign of the marred girdle

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Warning to the king; captivity foretold

chapters.title: Drought and False Comfort
chapters.synopsis: A great drought grips the land, and Jeremiah pleads for mercy though the people's sins testify against them. The Lord answers that the false prophets who promise peace and no famine speak lies, and sword and famine will consume them instead.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah's plea amid the drought

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: False prophets condemned; Jeremiah still pleads

chapters.title: Even Moses and Samuel Could Not Turn Judgment
chapters.synopsis: The Lord tells Jeremiah that even if Moses and Samuel stood before him, his mind could not be toward this people, for Manasseh's sins have sealed their doom of sword, famine, and captivity. Jeremiah laments his own contentious calling, and the Lord promises to make him a fenced brasen wall against his enemies.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Judgment fixed despite Moses and Samuel

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah's complaint; promised as a brasen wall

chapters.title: Forbidden Marriage, Promised Return
chapters.synopsis: The Lord forbids Jeremiah to marry or mourn in this place, a living sign of the death and exile coming upon Judah for forsaking him for idols. Yet beyond judgment the Lord promises to gather his people again from all the lands to which he will drive them, fulfilling an oath as sure as his name.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sign of forbidden marriage and mourning

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A future gathering promised

chapters.title: Cursed Is the Man That Trusteth in Man
chapters.synopsis: The Lord contrasts the man who trusts in flesh, a heath in the desert, with the one who trusts in the Lord, a tree planted by the waters that never fails. Jeremiah is sent to preach hallowing the sabbath at Jerusalem's gates, for the deceitful heart of man is known and searched by God alone.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Trust in man versus trust in the Lord

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Hallow the sabbath at Jerusalem's gates

chapters.title: The Potter and the Clay
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah watches a potter reworking marred clay into another vessel, and the Lord declares that as clay in the potter's hand, so is Israel in his hand to build or pluck up according to their turning. When the people plot against Jeremiah for his warnings, he pleads with the Lord to deliver him from their pit.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The potter's clay, a sign for Israel

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Plots against Jeremiah; his plea for justice

chapters.title: The Broken Earthen Bottle
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sends Jeremiah to buy a potter's bottle and break it before the elders in the valley of Hinnom, a sign that Jerusalem will be broken as a vessel that cannot be made whole again. Their sacrifice of children to Baal in that valley has provoked this coming desolation.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The bottle broken in the valley of Hinnom

chapters.title: Jeremiah's Burning Fire Shut Up in His Bones
chapters.synopsis: Struck and put in the stocks by the priest Pashur for his prophecy, Jeremiah cries out that the Lord's word is in his heart like a burning fire he cannot hold in. Torn between the derision he suffers and his inability to stay silent, he curses the day of his birth even while praising the Lord who delivers the poor from evildoers.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Pashur strikes Jeremiah and puts him in the stocks

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: A burning fire shut up in his bones

chapters.title: Zedekiah's Vain Inquiry
chapters.synopsis: King Zedekiah sends to ask whether the Lord will drive Nebuchadnezzar's besieging army away, but Jeremiah answers that the Lord himself fights against the city. Only those who go out and fall to the Chaldeans will save their lives, for the Lord sets before the house of David the way of life and the way of death.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Zedekiah's messengers inquire of Jeremiah

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The way of life and the way of death

chapters.title: Woe to the Unjust King
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands Jeremiah to warn the king's house at Jerusalem to execute justice and deliver the oppressed, or the palace will become a desolation. He pronounces doom on Shallum carried captive, on Jehoiakim who builds his house by unrighteousness, and on Coniah, who will be written childless as to sitting on David's throne.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Charge to execute judgment and righteousness

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Doom pronounced on Shallum, Jehoiakim, and Coniah

chapters.title: The Branch of Righteousness
chapters.synopsis: The Lord condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock and the prophets who prophesy lies out of their own hearts, yet promises to raise up a righteous Branch, a King who will reign and execute judgment. He warns that a true prophet has his word like a fire and a hammer, unlike those who steal words from one another and call it a burden of the Lord.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: False shepherds judged; the righteous Branch promised

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: False prophets rebuked; the word like fire and hammer

chapters.title: Two Baskets of Figs
chapters.synopsis: The Lord shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs before the temple, one good and one naught. The good figs represent the captives already carried to Babylon, whom the Lord will build up and give a heart to know him, while the naughty figs represent those left in Jerusalem, doomed to sword, famine, and pestilence.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Good figs and naughty figs, a sign of exile

chapters.title: Seventy Years of Servitude
chapters.synopsis: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, Jeremiah reminds the people that for twenty-three years the Lord's warnings have gone unheeded, and now Nebuchadnezzar will bring the whole land into servitude for seventy years. The Lord then sends a cup of his fury for all the nations to drink, for he will plead with all flesh and give the wicked to the sword.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Twenty-three years unheeded; seventy years of servitude

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The cup of fury given to all nations

chapters.title: Jeremiah on Trial for His Life
chapters.synopsis: Standing in the temple court, Jeremiah warns that Jerusalem will become like Shiloh if the people will not obey, and priests and prophets seize him demanding death. Princes and elders recall how Micah once prophesied similarly without harm, and Jeremiah is spared, though the prophet Urijah who spoke likewise is put to death.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Command to warn or Jerusalem becomes as Shiloh

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah seized, tried, and spared

chapters.title: The Yoke of Babylon
chapters.synopsis: The Lord has Jeremiah wear a wooden yoke and send word to the surrounding kings that all nations must serve Nebuchadnezzar or perish by sword and famine. False prophets promising a swift end to Babylon's dominion are exposed as liars, for the Lord's own vessels of the temple will only return when he appoints.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The sign of the yoke sent to the nations

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Submit to Babylon; false prophets exposed

chapters.title: Hananiah Breaks the Yoke
chapters.synopsis: The prophet Hananiah publicly breaks the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck, declaring that within two years the Lord will break Babylon's power and return the captives. Jeremiah answers that only the prophet whose word comes to pass is known as truly sent, and Hananiah dies that very year as Jeremiah foretold.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Hananiah breaks the yoke and prophesies falsely

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Yokes of iron; Hananiah's death foretold

chapters.title: Letter to the Exiles in Babylon
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah sends a letter to the elders and captives already carried to Babylon, urging them to build houses, plant gardens, and seek the peace of the city, for the Lord knows the thoughts he thinks toward them, thoughts of peace and an expected end after seventy years. He also condemns false prophets among the exiles, Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah, who deceive the people with lying visions.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Build houses; I know the thoughts I think toward you

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: False prophets among the exiles condemned

chapters.title: The Book of Israel's Restoration
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands Jeremiah to write in a book the promise that Israel and Judah will be brought back from captivity to possess their own land again. Though the day of Jacob's trouble is terrible, he will be saved out of it, and David's seed shall serve the Lord their God as their true King.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The book of Israel's future restoration

chapters.title: A New Covenant Written in the Heart
chapters.synopsis: The Lord promises to build again the virgin of Israel, gathering the blind, lame, and weeping exiles from the north country with mercies like a father to a firstborn son. He declares a new covenant, unlike the one broken at Sinai, that he will write in their inward parts, so that all shall know him, from the least to the greatest.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The scattered gathered with weeping and mercy

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: A new covenant written in their hearts

chapters.title: The Field Bought at Anathoth
chapters.synopsis: While Jerusalem is under siege and Jeremiah shut up in prison, the Lord directs him to buy his cousin Hanameel's field at Anathoth as a sign that houses and fields will again be bought in the land. Jeremiah prays acknowledging nothing is too hard for the Lord, who answers that though the city will fall for its wickedness, he will surely gather his people again and plant them in this land in truth.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah buys the field of Anathoth

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Nothing is too hard for thee

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Judgment now, gathering and planting later

chapters.title: Cities Shall Yet Be Inhabited
chapters.synopsis: Still in prison, Jeremiah hears the Lord promise to heal Jerusalem and reveal to her abundance of peace and truth, restoring the captivity of Judah and Israel and cleansing them from their iniquity. As surely as day and night keep their covenant order, the Lord's covenant with David's throne and the Levitical priesthood will not fail.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Healing and restoration; the covenant sure as day and night

chapters.title: Zedekiah Warned; Bondmen Freed and Re-enslaved
chapters.synopsis: The Lord tells Zedekiah he will see Nebuchadnezzar's face and die in peace despite Jerusalem's fall. The princes and people had covenanted to free their Hebrew slaves during the siege but afterward forced them back into bondage, so the Lord proclaims a liberty of sword, famine, and pestilence upon them instead.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Zedekiah's fate foretold

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Broken covenant of freed and re-enslaved servants

chapters.title: The Faithful Rechabites
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah brings the family of the Rechabites into the temple and offers them wine, but they refuse, keeping the ancient command of their father Jonadab to drink no wine and dwell in tents. The Lord holds up their obedience as a rebuke to Judah, who has ignored his repeated words, and promises the Rechabites shall never lack a man to stand before him.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The Rechabites refuse the wine

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Rechabite obedience contrasted with Judah's

chapters.title: The Scroll Read and Burned
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah dictates all the Lord's words to Baruch, who writes them on a scroll and reads them in the temple. When the scroll is read before King Jehoiakim, he cuts it apart with a penknife and casts it piece by piece into the fire, so the Lord commands Jeremiah to dictate it again with many similar words added.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Command to write all the words on a scroll

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jehoiakim burns the scroll in the fire

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The scroll rewritten with added words

chapters.title: Jeremiah Imprisoned
chapters.synopsis: King Zedekiah sends secretly asking Jeremiah to pray for the people as Pharaoh's army causes the Chaldeans to withdraw briefly, but Jeremiah warns the Egyptians will fail and the Chaldeans will return. Attempting to leave the city, Jeremiah is seized as a deserter, beaten, and shut up in a dungeon house, though Zedekiah later has him moved to a lighter prison court.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Zedekiah's request; Egypt's help will fail

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah seized, beaten, and imprisoned

chapters.title: Cast into the Miry Pit
chapters.synopsis: Princes accuse Jeremiah of weakening the defenders' hands and have him lowered into a muddy dungeon pit to die, but the Ethiopian Ebed-melech pleads with the king and draws him out with old rags and cords. Zedekiah secretly consults Jeremiah again, who urges surrender to Babylon to save the city and his own life, but the king fears his own people and does not obey.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Cast into the pit; Ebed-melech rescues him

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Zedekiah's secret counsel; the king's fear

chapters.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
chapters.synopsis: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the Chaldeans break through Jerusalem's wall, and the fleeing king is captured near Jericho, his sons slain before his eyes before he himself is blinded and carried to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar's captain shows kindness to Jeremiah, releasing him, while Ebed-melech is promised his life as a reward for trusting the Lord.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The city falls; Zedekiah captured and blinded

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah released; Ebed-melech promised deliverance

chapters.title: Jeremiah Remains in the Land
chapters.synopsis: Freed from his chains at Ramah, Jeremiah chooses to remain in the land with Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon has set as governor over the remnant. Gedaliah counsels the scattered captains to serve the Chaldeans and dwell safely, but Johanan warns him in vain of a plot against his life by Ishmael.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jeremiah freed and remains with Gedaliah

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Gedaliah governs; a plot against him is reported

chapters.title: Gedaliah Slain
chapters.synopsis: Ishmael, of the royal seed, murders Gedaliah and many others at Mizpah, then casts their bodies into a pit and takes captive the remaining people. Johanan pursues and rescues the captives from Ishmael, who escapes to the Ammonites, and the remnant flees toward Egypt for fear of Chaldean reprisal.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Gedaliah murdered; the remnant flees toward Egypt

chapters.title: Dwell Not in Egypt
chapters.synopsis: Johanan and the remaining captains ask Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord whether to flee to Egypt, vowing to obey whatever answer comes. After ten days the Lord answers that if they remain in the land he will build them up, but if they go to Egypt the sword and famine they fear will overtake them there.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The remnant asks Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Remain in the land; Egypt brings the feared judgment

chapters.title: Flight into Egypt
chapters.synopsis: Refusing Jeremiah's counsel, Johanan and the proud men carry the remnant, along with Jeremiah and Baruch, down into Egypt to Tahpanhes. The Lord tells Jeremiah to hide stones before Pharaoh's house as a sign that Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne there and smite the land of Egypt.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The remnant defies counsel and flees to Egypt

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Sign of stones; Nebuchadnezzar to smite Egypt

chapters.title: Judgment on the Refugees in Egypt
chapters.synopsis: Jeremiah rebukes the Jews in Egypt for continuing to burn incense to the queen of heaven and other gods, provoking the same wrath that destroyed Jerusalem. The people defiantly answer that they fared better when they worshipped the queen of heaven, so the Lord vows that this remnant in Egypt will be consumed until none remain, save a small escaped few.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Rebuke for continued idolatry in Egypt

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The people's defiance; judgment renewed

chapters.title: A Word of Comfort to Baruch
chapters.synopsis: When Baruch grieves over the sorrow added to his pain in writing Jeremiah's words of doom, the Lord tells him not to seek great things for himself amid the coming destruction. Yet his life will be given him as a prize wherever he goes, a promise of preservation amid judgment.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Comfort and preservation promised to Baruch

chapters.title: Against Egypt at Carchemish
chapters.synopsis: The Lord's word against Egypt describes Pharaoh-necho's army routed at Carchemish by the king of Babylon, fleeing in terror though armed and prepared. Yet after judgment falls, Jacob is promised he will again be at rest and quiet, none making him afraid.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Egypt routed at Carchemish

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Jacob promised future rest

chapters.title: Against the Philistines
chapters.synopsis: As waters rise out of the north like an overflowing flood, the Lord's word comes against the Philistines, foretelling the spoiling of Gaza and the cutting off of Tyre and Zidon's help. Fathers will have no strength to help their children in that day of desolation.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Flood from the north against the Philistines

chapters.title: The Judgment of Moab
chapters.synopsis: The Lord pronounces extensive judgment on Moab, at ease from her youth and settled on her lees, now to be emptied from vessel to vessel and brought low for magnifying herself against the Lord. Yet even for Moab the Lord promises to bring again her captivity in the latter days.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Moab's pride brought low

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Moab's captivity to be reversed in the latter days

chapters.title: Judgments on Ammon, Edom, and Nations
chapters.synopsis: The Lord pronounces judgment in turn on Ammon for occupying Gad's inheritance, on Edom for pride in the clefts of the rock, and on Damascus, Kedar, Hazor, and Elam for their false confidence. Yet even Ammon and Elam are promised a future restoration of their captivity.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Ammon and Edom judged for pride

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Damascus, Kedar, Hazor, and Elam judged

chapters.title: The Fall of Babylon Foretold
chapters.synopsis: The Lord announces that Babylon, the golden cup that made all the earth drunken, will itself be taken and utterly destroyed by a nation out of the north, while Israel and Judah, lost sheep long led astray, will be sought and forgiven and return to Zion. Babylon's own idols and mighty men will fail her in the day the Lord repays her for what she did to his sanctuary.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Babylon's fall; Israel's sins forgiven

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: The destroyer comes upon Babylon

chapters.title: Babylon's Utter Destruction
chapters.synopsis: The Lord raises up a destroying wind against Babylon, the golden cup and hammer of the whole earth, now to be recompensed for all the blood shed in Zion. Jeremiah instructs that this prophecy be read in Babylon and then sunk with a stone in the Euphrates, a sign that Babylon shall sink and rise no more.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: Babylon recompensed for the blood of Zion

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: The scroll sunk in the Euphrates as a sign

chapters.title: Historical Appendix: The Fall of Jerusalem Retold
chapters.synopsis: This closing appendix retells in careful detail the reign of Zedekiah, the siege and fall of Jerusalem, the burning of the temple, and the exile of the people to Babylon, with exact counts of those carried away in three deportations. It ends with Jehoiachin, long a captive, lifted up and given a place of honor at the Babylonian king's table.

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Zedekiah's reign and the fall of the city

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Temple vessels taken; the deportation counts

segments.speaker: jeremiah
segments.note: Jehoiachin lifted up in Babylon
